speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether more measures can be put in place to detect non-compliant active mobility devices (AMDs) considering the increased incidence of AMD-related fires in 2024; (b) whether enforcement officers are adequately trained to identify modifications on non-compliant AMDs during spot-checks; (c) whether the frequency of spot checks on shops that repair or sell AMDs can be increased; and (d) whether more stringent penalties can be imposed to deter illegal modifications, especially for repeat offenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Our officers undergo regular training to be updated on the latest violation trends, and are equipped with a variety of detection tools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Most recently, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) conducted an ambush operation in Punggol and seized four non-compliant AMDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will continue to conduct regular and targeted enforcement operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Third, we require e-scooters, which are required to be registered for use, to undergo inspections every two years to ensure compliance with regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Fourth, we impose significant penalties on illegal modifications of AMDs for deterrence, given the risks they pose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: All offenders, including first-time offenders, will be taken to court.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Repeat offenders are liable for higher fines and/or imprisonment terms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will continue to review regulations relating to AMDs, to enhance fire safety and deter the sale, purchase and use of non-compliant devices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have several Yio Chu Kang residents coming to me, expressing concerns about AMDs and fires related to AMDs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Considering the role that retailers, repair shops and especially online shops play in the modification and maintenance of AMDs, how does the Ministry determine the current frequency of inspections for these establishments?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What criteria are being used to assess compliance and are there plans to increase inspection frequency or implement additional measures to ensure adherence to safety standards?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And lastly, what is being done to ensure compliance of safe devices being sold by online retailers?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In particular, for retailer operations, the number of operations mounted over the years has increased; in fact, it has increased four-folds, in 2022 compared to 2024.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will share more later this year and we hope that this would help us in our efforts against sale, purchase and use of non-compliant devices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask MOT whether as part of the regulation review, they will be looking at how liability is assigned when a device has been purchased from an online shop, and let us say subsequently, there is a fire.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In short, does the Ministry agree that the liability should not be any different regardless of whether the item was bought from an online retailer or from an offline, brick and mortar real world retailer?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because the fire burns as hot and as damaging, regardless of where the defective product came from.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: When we look at reviewing the regulations against online retailers, we look at how we can align the rules that we apply on brick and mortar retailers as well.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: If a retailer knowingly sells a non-compliant device or an illegally modified device, the retailer must be held responsible.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But if the purchaser subsequently modifies the device, then the purchaser or the owner of the device must be responsible.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In cases where we are able to investigate and conclude which is the party that is responsible for the illegal modifications, the relevant party will be taken to task.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned about actions against retailers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In the past, I believe in the previous Committees of Supply or Bills, I have suggested for the Government to take action at the Customs level, when retailers import illegal AMDs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can I ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to update the House on what efforts are being taken to stop the import of illegal AMDs at our border?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Whether in terms of fire risk or when they are in use generally in the public, for example.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Because we still see that there are many non-compliant devices being used on the road, for example, those using throttle or those with weight issues and also illegal speed modification, and bearing in mind that LTA will also be requiring more resources soon as they seek to enforce the new regulations on mobility scooters.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we work with our border agencies to do that.
